nffe01.title: The friend who went quiet
nffe01.caption: When a friend goes quiet, it is easy to assume it is about you. Often it isn't. Send a check-in with no homework attached: thinking of you, no need to reply.

nffe02.title: Check-in, not a quiz
nffe02.caption: Six questions in a row can feel like a test, even when they come from love. Ask one soft question, then let the quiet do some of the work. Save this for the next time you're worried about a friend.

nffe03.title: December is hard for some friends
nffe03.caption: Not everyone loves this month, especially in a year when someone is missing. You don't have to fix it. Ask if they want company or quiet, and make room for both.

nffe04.title: The plan you can say no to
nffe04.caption: The kindest invites come with an easy way out. Pyjamas welcome, leave whenever, no is totally fine. When saying no is easy, saying yes gets a little easier too.

nffe05.title: The cancelled-plans friend
nffe05.caption: Third cancellation and the scorecard is already drafted. Skip it. Say how it felt once, kindly, then ask what's going on with them. Sometimes the answer is just: I'm overbooked.

nffe06.title: Long-distance friends
nffe06.caption: Different cities, different clocks, a lot of missed calls. A small ritual beats a perfect plan: one time, every week, kept. Who would you set a standing call with?

nffe07.title: Who checks on the checker?
nffe07.caption: The friend who always listens rarely gets asked how they are. Turn the question around tonight, and then actually wait for the answer. Tag the friend who holds everyone up.

nffe08.title: Show up with soup
nffe08.caption: When a friend is sick, the best care asks nothing back. Leave the soup at the door, send one line, and let them rest without having to host you.

nffe09.title: Good news, shared
nffe09.caption: Hiding good news to protect a struggling friend can leave them out of something lovely. Friends can hold both. Share it gently and let them choose to celebrate with you.

nffe10.title: When a friend is in a new relationship
nffe10.caption: A friend in love can disappear for a while. "You've changed" pushes them away; "we miss you" invites them back. Say it warmly, and leave room for the new person too.

nffe11.title: The tiny check-in
nffe11.caption: No energy for a paragraph? You don't need one. A ten-second voice note or one honest line still tells your friends you're here. Small check-ins count.

nffe12.title: Boundaries with friends
nffe12.caption: You can love someone and still not have anything left at 1 AM. A boundary is care for both of you. Say the no, offer the next yes, and show up rested.

nffe13.title: Far away for the holidays
nffe13.caption: When a friend can't come home this year, send something they can hold. One envelope, a note from each of you, in your own handwriting. Far is not the same as forgotten.

nffe14.title: The hard date on the calendar
nffe14.caption: Some days stay heavy every year. Remembering one for a friend is a quiet kind of love. A short message, no pressure to reply, can mean more than you'd guess.

nffe15.title: The new friend in the group
nffe15.caption: Inside jokes are fun until someone is standing outside them. When a new friend joins, explain the story and let them in on it. It's how a group gets bigger without anyone feeling left out.

nffe16.title: When your friend says I'm fine
nffe16.caption: Sometimes fine means fine, and sometimes it means not yet. Don't push and don't disappear. Let them know you're there if fine changes, and keep that door open.

nffe17.title: Let your friends help
nffe17.caption: If you're always the one who handles everything alone, this is for you. Letting friends help is a gift to them too. One word is enough to start: help?

nffe18.title: The weekly check-in
nffe18.caption: One small ritual can make honesty normal in a friend group: every Sunday, one good thing and one hard thing. It makes the hard things easier to say. Would your group chat try it?

nffe19.title: The friend who's alone this year
nffe19.caption: "Come by sometime" is easy to turn down. A day, a time and a seat with their name on it is much harder to refuse. Be specific with the friend spending the holidays alone.

nffe20.title: Thank your friend
nffe20.caption: "Thanks for everything" is sweet. "Thank you for every Tuesday call this year" lands differently. Name the specific thing your friend did, then let them cry about it.

nffe21.title: Quiet company
nffe21.caption: When a friend doesn't want to talk, you don't need the perfect words. Sit with them, find an edge piece, stay for the hour. Being there is a whole sentence.

nffe22.title: Talk cards at friends' night
nffe22.caption: One real question can turn a night of jokes into a night that matters. Ask what made your friends proud this year, then give the honest answer the room it deserves.

nffe23.title: After the holidays
nffe23.caption: The quiet days after the holidays can be harder than the holidays themselves. Check in after too: how are you doing now that it's quiet? Someone will be glad you asked.

nffe24.title: The year's last friends' night
nffe24.caption: A year of small check-ins adds up to this: the whole group in one room, and one more on the call. Thank you for being someone's friend first. Who are you sending this to?
